title: Chananiah bar Idi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Pesachim 105a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.105a): Rav Shmuel bar Idi sent to them, “Chananiah my brother says one” (and the halakhah does not follow him). Were I not afraid, I would say that it should read that Rav Shmuel bar Idi sent: “Chananiah [son of] the brother of [R' Yehoshua] says one.” And, as they said there at the end of the page, it was taught in the name of ריב״ח—and the halakhah does not follow him. The matter requires further study.[^1]

notes.text: The tentative proposed reading and the brackets [son of] and [R' Yehoshua] belong to Hyman, not to a new correction here. שר״ש בר אידי is expanded contextually from the preceding full Rav Shmuel bar Idi; the personal abbreviation in דריב״ח remains unresolved, with the initial ד translated as “of.” The old invented “Rabbi Yishmael ben Yochai” is withdrawn. שצ״ל and צ״ע are the ordinary expressions “it should read” and “requires further study.” “Says one” is left as the quoted fragment because the notice supplies no object. The printed locator קה. is conventionally 105a and was not independently verified.

Hyman’s bracketed ר׳ יהושע is retained as [R' Yehoshua], preserving his brackets while leaving the title unresolved. The full רב שמואל in the opening report is retained; the later contextual expansion of שר״ש remains tied to that same preceding wording. The title inside the withdrawn old English name in note 1 is quoted only to identify the rejected reading.
